en-GB.name: Snapjaw
en-GB.subtitle: Feed the flytrap. Spare bees.
en-GB.description:
Your iPhone Duo is a Venus flytrap.

Hold your Duo open like a book. The two halves are the trap's lobes and the hinge is its midrib. Bugs fly in and land on the glistening nectar to sip. But bees love nectar too, and you must never eat a bee.

The trick is choosing your moment. Wait for a crowd, then snap the phone a little shut and the trap bites with you: CHOMP. Every bug inside is caught in one bite, and your score is multiplied by the number of bugs. Then open it again and wait.

No ads. No in-app purchases. No accounts. No data collected. Pay once and it's yours.

PATIENCE, GREED AND BEES
• Snaps are what you spend. A run starts with 10 (a few more in your first runs), you hold up to 14, and every snap costs one
• Catch 3 or more bugs in one bite for a Feast and win a snap back. Catch 5 or more for a big FEAST: the bugs are gulped one by one and two snaps come back
• Score = the bugs' points × the number of bugs × your chain
• Every clean bite of 2 or more bugs grows the chain, all the way to ×5. An empty snap or a bee in the bite starts it again
• A bee in the bite is let go, unharmed and cross, and costs an extra snap. A wasp stings: two extra
• Sipping bugs are distracted. Flying ones are quick. Close too slowly and the twitchy ones leave
• Keep a bug waiting too long and a snap wilts
• When the snaps run out, your trap is tired. One more go?

GOALS AND GROWTH
Three goals are always on the go, from a pool of 39: a 5-bug bite, spare 8 bees in one run, catch a firefly at night, and many more. Each one you complete grows your plant and makes way for a new one; all three in one run earns a bonus. Your plant climbs 12 ranks, from Sprout to Bog Monarch.

THE GARDEN
Grow 8 flytraps: Classic, Red Dragon, B52, Sawtooth, Shark Tooth, Fused Tooth, Cupped Trap and, for a Bog Monarch only, Golden Glow. Some grow as you rank up; others are won with a special goal. Pick one and it's your trap in every run. Same bite, new look.

A DAY IN THE BOG
Every run moves from morning to night, and the bugs change with the light: houseflies and gnats at breakfast, ladybirds and grasshoppers by noon, moths and dragonflies at dusk, fireflies and crickets in the dark, and now and then a rare Golden Scarab.

THE BUG BOOK
16 species, each with a drawing and a one-line joke. Catch a bug to add its page; bees and wasps go in when you spare them.

DAILY BOG
The same bugs for everyone, every day, and one try that counts. Play day after day to grow your streak, and share your score with friends. Then practise as much as you like.

ZEN BOG
No rush, no end. Snaps never run out, nothing wilts, and a bee costs you nothing but your chain. Catch at your own pace, fill the Bug Book, and stop whenever you like. No leaderboard.

FIRST BITE
Your first go starts with a short lesson that teaches by doing. Replay it from Settings any time.

MADE FOR THE FOLD. PLAYS ON OTHER iPhone MODELS TOO.
On iPhone Duo, the hinge is the trap: a short snap of about 22° from however you like to hold it, then open again. You never close the phone or lay it flat, and the bite happens at 22°, so there is nothing to gain by going further. iPhone Duo softens one half of the screen for a moment when a fold starts from flat, so your score and snaps sit on the half that stays sharp (Settings can move them). On any other iPhone, tap anywhere to snap.

SOUND AND FEEL
The CHOMP, every buzz and hum, the frogs by day and the crickets at night are all synthesised live in the app, and a big FEAST gets its own crunch and a burp. You feel a soft tick in your hands when a bug lands. Sound, haptics, the silent switch and Reduce motion each have a setting.

GAME CENTER
Leaderboards for your Best Score and the Daily Bog, and 12 achievements. Optional: Snapjaw works fully without signing in.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No accounts, no tracking, no data collected. Your progress stays on your iPhone.
en-GB.promotionalText: Your iPhone Duo is a Venus flytrap. Wait for a crowd, snap it a little shut and never eat a bee. Then grow 8 flytraps, chase goals or relax in the Zen Bog.

review.notes:
Thanks for reviewing Snapjaw: a paid game with no ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts, no data collection and no network requests of its own.

1. TESTING WITHOUT AN iPHONE DUO (start here)
You don't need a Duo. It all works on any iPhone, iPad (as an iPhone app) and the Simulator, in landscape.
- Control: tap anywhere to snap the trap. It opens again by itself.
- The first launch starts First Bite, a short lesson: tap while the fly is sipping. Skip appears after the second step; Settings > Replay First Bite plays it again.
- Quickest look (about a minute): two lesson steps, Skip, then Feed on Home.
- In Feed, bugs land on the gold nectar drops. A tap catches every bug inside the trap at once. Score = the bugs' points x the number of bugs x the chain (up to x5, grown by bites of 2+ bugs), so waiting for a crowd pays.
- Bees, bumblebees and wasps wear a white halo. Never eat them: a bee in a bite is let go unharmed and costs an extra snap.
- A run starts with 10 snaps (12 to 14 in a new player's first three runs), holds at most 14, and each snap costs 1. 3+ bugs in one bite (a Feast) earns snaps back. At 0, "Your trap is tired" and the results show the score.

2. HOW THE HINGE IS USED (iPhone Duo)
Snapjaw reads the hinge angle only through the public iOS 27.1 API (SwiftUI onHingeChange), behind an availability check. No private API. The angle is used only while playing and is never sent anywhere.
a) Hold the Duo open like a book (landscape, fold top to bottom), relaxed, anywhere from about 135 to 175 degrees. The game follows the player's own resting angle.
b) To snap, close the halves about 22 degrees from that rest, then open again. The bite is decided at 22 degrees, so going further gains nothing and nothing is held. A very slow close never bites and lets twitchy bugs leave.
c) The score, snaps and hints sit on the right half, which stays sharp when iOS briefly softens one half as a fold starts from flat. Settings > Score on the left moves them.
d) Below about 50 degrees for half a second, the run pauses with a card. Closed, the outer display shows a card. Portrait shows a pose card.
e) Nearly flat only shows a hint: "Bend it a little, like a book". No penalty.

3. KIND TO THE DEVICE (Guidelines 2.4.2 and 1.4.5)
- Every snap is a short stroke of about 22 to 40 degrees from a relaxed book pose. Snapjaw never asks the user to close the phone, lay it flat or slam it.
- Snaps are limited (10 to start, 14 at most), so the game rewards waiting, not snapping often: a run is about 25 to 40 snaps over 2 to 3 minutes. The Zen Bog has no limit and no timer.
- No achievement, goal or leaderboard rewards snap speed or snap count.

4. MODES AND PROGRESS (nothing hidden, nothing to buy)
- Feed: endless waves from morning to night, until the snaps run out.
- Daily Bog: the same bugs for everyone; one scored try a day, then practice. A streak counts the days in a row; Share opens the iOS share sheet with one line (score, biggest bite, streak).
- Zen Bog: relaxed and endless; snaps never run out, nothing wilts, no leaderboard. Pause > End shows the results.
- Goals: three at a time on Home, from 39. A completed goal grows the plant rank and is replaced.
- Garden: 8 cosmetic flytraps, unlocked by rank or by a goal. Same rules.
- Bug Book: 16 species. Plant rank: 12 cosmetic ranks.

5. CONTENT
A cartoon Venus flytrap catching cartoon bugs, the way a frog catches flies. No blood or injury: caught bugs are gulped into the trap, and bees and wasps are always let go unharmed.

6. PRIVACY
No third-party SDKs, analytics, ads, accounts or tracking. Progress and settings stay on the device; Share sends nothing itself. App Privacy: Data Not Collected.

7. GAME CENTER
Optional. 2 leaderboards (Best Score, Daily Bog; Zen submits none), 12 achievements (575 points), none hidden.

8. OTHER
- No notifications. Debug and demo modes are disabled in Release builds.
- Sound plays with the silent switch on; Settings > Respect silent switch turns that off.

nomination.name: Snapjaw - App Launch - iPhone Duo Venus flytrap game
nomination.description:
Snapjaw turns iPhone Duo into a Venus flytrap. Hold the Duo open like a book: the two halves are the trap's lobes and the hinge is its midrib. Bugs land on the glistening nectar to sip; snap the phone a little shut and the trap bites with you, teeth clacking together, then open it again.

It's a game of choosing, not hitting. Wait for a crowd and catch them all in one bite, for a score multiplied by the number of bugs, but bees love nectar too and must never be eaten. Snaps are the resource, and big bites earn them back. Every run passes from morning to night with new bugs, from houseflies to dragonflies and fireflies, and a Bug Book of 16 species to fill.

Three goals at a time grow your plant through 12 ranks, and a Garden of 8 flytraps rewards them. A Daily Bog with a streak, a Zen Bog that never ends, a First Bite lesson and Game Center. Other iPhones play by tapping. Every sound is synthesized in the app. No ads, no in-app purchases, no data collected.
nomination.notes: Optimized for iPhone Duo: built for book pose on the inner display. Public iOS 27.1 hinge API: a snap is a short close of about 22 degrees from the player's own resting angle, never flat and never shut, and the bite fires at 22 degrees, so closing further gains nothing. The score stays on the half that doesn't blur when a fold starts from flat. Snaps are a limited resource, so patience beats folding often. Taught by doing. Also from us: Squish, Brim, Swoop and Hush.
